source_text:
Fragmenta precationis et exorcismi
Ἐπικαλούμεθά σε, Θεὲ παντοκράτορ Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ οὐράνιε βασιλεῦ·
ἐπικαλούμεθά σε τὸν ποιήσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν. Ἐξορκίζω σε, πνεῦμα
ἀκάθαρτον, κατὰ τοῦ λόγου Θεοῦ τοῦ ποιήσαντος τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν.
φοβήθητι τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον φῶς ὡς ἱμάτιον· τὸν μόνον ἔχοντα ἀθανασίαν καὶ
φῶς ἀπρόσιτον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Invocation and Exorcism of an Unclean Spirit
orientation: The exorcist opens the fragment by calling upon God the Almighty, the Lord Jesus Christ, the heavenly king, and upon the maker of heaven and earth, then commands an unclean spirit by the word of God.
pass_a_gloss: We call upon you, God Almighty, Lord Jesus Christ, heavenly king; we call upon you, the [one] having made the heaven and the earth. I command you, unclean spirit, by the word of God, the [one] having made the heaven and the earth. Fear the [one] clothing [himself with] light as [with] a garment; the only [one] having immortality and unapproachable light; to whom [be] the glory and the dominion unto the ages. Amen.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'we call upon' for this invocation verb, avoiding 'we invoke'.
Glossary requires 'I command' for the exorcism verb, avoiding 'I adjure' or 'I exorcize'.

choices.english: the one who is clothed with light as with a garment
choices.why: Glossary requires this exact rendering for the biblical image of God's glory.
rejected: who is arrayed in light as in a garment
who puts on light as a cloak

choices.why: Glossary requires 'unapproachable light' for this divine attribute.
Glossary requires 'dominion' for this doxological term, avoiding 'might' or 'power'.

bible_refs.note: ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν, φῶς ἀπρόσιτον

pass_b_english: We call upon you, God Almighty, Lord Jesus Christ, heavenly king. We call upon you, the maker of heaven and earth.

I command you, unclean spirit, by the word of God who made heaven and earth: fear the one who is clothed with light as with a garment (Psalm 104:2), the one alone having immortality and unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16).
To him be glory and dominion forever. Amen.

problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered two ways; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use consistent wording across all sections.

variants.text: the only one who has immortality

problems.quote: We call upon you, God Almighty
problems.why: Unclear who 'we' is until intro explains; shift to 'I command' unexplained in text.
problems.fix: Note speaker shift in heading or margin.

problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered two different ways across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Standardize to one rendering across all sections.

variants.text: the only one who has immortality

edits.new: the one who alone has immortality

fixed: The speaker shift is already clear from the paragraph break and the first-person singular 'I command you'; no change needed.
The glossary problem is addressed by standardizing the English rendering to 'the one who alone has immortality'.

problems.quote: the one who alone has immortality
problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered three ways; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Standardize to one English rendering across all recensions.

variants.text: the one who alone has immortality

problems.quote: We call upon you, God Almighty
problems.why: Sudden shift from plural 'we' to singular 'I command' with no explanation of who speaks.
problems.fix: Note the liturgical 'we' shifts to exorcist's 'I'.

problems.quote: the one who alone has immortality
problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered three different ways across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Standardize to one rendering across all parallel sections.

variants.text: the one who alone has immortality

problems.quote: the maker of heaven and earth
problems.why: Same title rendered as noun phrase vs. relative clause in parallel sections.
problems.fix: Use one consistent rendering across all parallel sections.

variants.text: the maker of heaven and earth

edits.old: the maker of heaven and earth
edits.new: the one who made heaven and earth

edits.old: the one who alone has immortality

fixed: The speaker shift from plural 'we call upon' to singular 'I command' is inherent in the source and is not a translation error; no change made.
The Greek phrase for 'the one who made heaven and earth' is now rendered consistently as 'the one who made heaven and earth' in both occurrences.
The Greek phrase for 'the only one having immortality' is now rendered consistently as 'the only one having immortality'.
